source.citation: Akhil Ayyadevara et al., Symmetry-Controlled Thermal Activation in Pyramidal Coulomb Clusters: Testing Kramers-Langer Theory, Physical Review Letters (2026), DOI:10.1103/xsdn-srjd

assessment: The paper provides a useful qualitative mechanism contrast between identical-ion pseudo-rotation and isotope-substituted turnstile rotation, but it does not report two executable inversion-rate branches over a shared active domain. The isotope branch is qualitative at one approximate aspect ratio, while the Kramers-Langer branch requires source quantities not represented as executable functions or parameters in the ScienceCard.

issues.detail: The identical-ion response is discussed across the bistable aspect-ratio range, whereas the isotope-substituted comparison is only a qualitative observation at alpha approximately 1.09. The source does not provide both inversion-rate branches on a common nonzero alpha interval.

The Kramers-Langer rate requires the alpha-dependent barrier, Hessian determinants, positive saddle eigenvalue and damping. The card contains only the multiplicity N=4; the source gives only an illustrative incomplete spectrum and approximate barriers, not the functions and parameters needed for arbitrary in-domain queries.
The paper-native branches are pseudo-rotation and turnstile rotation, but the card extracts only generic Kramers-Langer and Langevin mechanisms and supplies no quantitative isotope-branch rate law.

The card writes the experimental rate below threshold as equal to the Kramers-Langer rate. The source states that the excess rate follows Kramers-Langer and separately retains a background-collision offset, so the proposed exact piecewise equality is not source faithful.

The source defines rate extraction and sample sizes for MD and identical-ion experiments, but the isotope branch is only a real-time qualitative trace with no numeric rate relation, uncertainty or shared-domain statistic.
